defects: The last ~4 s are almost static: per-second change falls to 6–15. The 4.7 s closing shot on 'loam' is dead air, with only the roots drifting.

In the pairs, held shots show near-identical frames 1/6 s apart: tiny camera pushes and almost no secondary motion on leaves, roots or water.
The soil-only shot (water drop on a flat brown field) is a near-empty frame with no subject, too weak to hold as a poster.

gaps: Motion has no physical weight or follow-through. Water, leaves and roots should react with overlap and settle (water sloshing, leaves drooping and recovering, roots growing with ease-out), not slow pushes and dissolves.

The energy arc is front-loaded: the peak is around 5–6 s (~40%), then a long tail. The transition into the cross-section and the 'loam' reveal should be choreographed as a built climax with a hard hit, then a short hold of under 1.5 s.

Sound is dense, heavily compressed and wall-to-wall, with one dropout at ~10.5 s. It needs dynamic range and specific sound design (the water pour, the drip, soil, the phone tap) instead of a constant rhythmic bed. The type should also take on meaning, e.g. the waterline physically setting the type baseline.
